podcast.body: This song, written by James Brown and Johnny Terry, was based on something Little Richard had scribbled on a napkin, which Brown saw potential in as a title. It fit a specific genre of R&B ballad, influenced by songs like Flow Example Richards' "Directly from My Heart to You," Fay Adams' "Shake a Hand," and The Orioles' version of Big Joe Williams' "Baby Please Don't Go," from which Brown borrowed the backing vocal arrangement. The emotional intensity of Brown's singing on this track was particularly effective, resonating with a type of woman who felt sympathy for him. The song reached number six on the R&B chart and reportedly sold between one and three million copies, though record companies often inflated sales figures at the time. "Bass was absolutely convinced that please, please, please would be a hit and championed the flames in the face of opposition from his boss, Sid Nathan."
